name: Zillapi
tagline: One REST call returns price, Zestimate, photos, schools, taxes and full history for any US home.

pricing.basis: pay per successful call, starts free with 100 credits
pricing.notes: No card to start; per-endpoint credit cost.

verdictSummary: This one is not about code, it is about data you do not have. The product is structured access to Zillow's 160M-property dataset (Zestimate, price history, tax and school data) delivered without scraping. You can write a Zillow scraper in an afternoon; it gets IP-blocked and captcha-walled almost immediately, and even when it works you are reconstructing one page at a time a dataset that is the whole point. There is no open Zillow dataset to build against. The value is the data plus the infrastructure to reach it, not the parsing.
coreLoopDIY: Scrape a Zillow listing page and parse out price, beds, baths and address.
diyTimeEstimate: one sitting for a fragile version
requirements: ongoing maintenance as Zillow changes markup and defenses
whatYouLose: the 160M-property dataset itself, which you cannot recreate
staying unblocked against active anti-bot defenses
300+ normalized fields per property in one call
Zestimate, tax history and school data you would have to source separately
any uptime the day Zillow changes its page structure
moatType: proprietary data access plus anti-blocking infrastructure
whyPeopleStillPay: The hard part was never parsing HTML. It is holding a durable, unblocked pipe into a dataset a large company spends heavily to protect, and normalizing 300+ fields so one call answers the question. That is an operations and access problem, not a coding problem.
notes: The scraper is a weekend build; the dataset behind it is not.
prompt: Build a tiny FastAPI service that returns basic data for a US home given a Zillow listing URL. Stack: Python 3.11, FastAPI, httpx, selectolax, uvicorn, no database. Endpoint: GET /property?url=... fetches the page and returns JSON { address, price, beds, baths, sqft } parsed from the listing. Set a real browser User-Agent, handle a missing field as null rather than crashing, and return 502 with a clear JSON error when the fetch is blocked or the markup has changed. Read an optional comma-separated PROXIES env var and rotate per request. Include a /health endpoint, a README, and a .env.example. Be honest in the README that this breaks under Zillow's anti-bot defenses at any real volume and does not reproduce Zestimate, tax, school or history data. Deliberately out of scope: a proxy pool you do not own, the full 300+ field schema, and any dataset you do not have rights to.
